level_1: Obtains an accurate history
level_2: Obtains and reports an accurate, organized history, and seeks appropriate data from secondary sources
level_3: Consistently obtains and reports a comprehensive and accurate history incorporating clinical patterns in historical data
level_4: Consistently obtains and concisely reports a focused history with subtle details supportive of a rational clinical diagnosis
level_5: Consistently serves as a role model and educator in obtaining and presenting a focused history with subtle details

level_1: Performs a basic physical exam accurately
level_2: Performs and reports an accurate, organized physical exam, and identifies appropriate physical findings for the chief complaint
level_3: Consistently performs an accurate and thorough physical examination, and reports relevant findings in support of likely clinical diagnosis
level_4: Consistently identifies and concisely reports subtle physical findings; is proficient with advanced maneuvers
level_5: Consistently serves as a role model and educator in the performance of an advanced physical exam

level_1: Integrates patient- specific information to generate an appropriate working diagnosis
level_2: Provides a prioritized differential diagnosis using supporting rationale
level_3: Consistently provides an accurate diagnosis for common medical conditions; demonstrates the ability to modify a diagnosis based on a patient’s clinical course and additional data
level_4: Consistently provides an accurate diagnosis for patients with multiple co-morbidities or uncommon medical conditions, recognizing sources of diagnostic error
level_5: Consistently serves as a role model and educator for deriving accurate diagnoses and recognizing sources of diagnostic error

level_1: With direct supervision, determines appropriate tests and initiates a therapeutic plan
level_2: With direct supervision, orders appropriate tests, and initiates a therapeutic plan; provides rational basis for decisions
level_3: With indirect supervision, orders appropriate tests, and initiates a therapeutic plan; provides rational basis for decisions
level_4: Consistently modifies the therapeutic plan based on test results and the patient’s clinical course as appropriate
level_5: Implements testing and therapeutic plans, integrating patient preferences, evidence- based guidelines, and costs

level_1: Recognizes urgent and emergent medical conditions and initiates system protocols as appropriate
Uses code status in clinical decision making
level_2: Knows code status
Coordinates the initial assessment and management of urgent and emergent conditions with the interprofessional care team
level_3: Performs an initial assessment of patients with urgent and emergent conditions
Considers patient and family wishes to modify code status and subsequent care as appropriate
level_4: Discusses and clarifies code status with patient and family
Anticipates clinical decompensation and intervenes early
level_5: Provides initial stabilization of patients with urgent and emergent medical conditions, as well as safe transitions in care
Leads conversation with medical team when care is futile

level_1: Describes basic health needs of heterogeneous patient populations
level_2: Addresses health needs of individual patient populations
level_3: Provides anticipatory guidance for health needs of individual patient populations
level_4: Teaches peers and/or students on health needs of individual patient populations
level_5: Advocates in the community for health needs of individual patient populations

level_1: Uses educational resources to answer clinical questions and to recognize gaps in personal medical knowledge
level_2: Integrates basic science knowledge, interpretation of test results, and social and behavioral determinants of health into clinical decision making
level_3: Incorporates preferences from patients, family, and interprofessional team into clinical decision making
level_4: Develops a rational treatment approach in ambiguous medical and/or social situations
level_5: Consistently serves as a role model and educator in the navigation of complex and ambiguous clinical decision making

level_1: Describes indications/ contraindications and complications of common procedures
Incorporates patient preferences in procedural decision making; assesses patient understanding
level_2: Describes informed consent process
Recognizes and provides initial management of complications
level_3: Accurately documents procedures in medical record in a timely manner
Describes procedural appropriateness in the context of the patient’s clinical scenario, addressing patient concerns
level_4: Counsels patients and obtains informed consent for common diagnostic and therapeutic procedures
Anticipates potential complications and discusses with attending
level_5: Demonstrates knowledge of indicated follow-up measures after procedures and recognizes common complications
Discusses potential treatment progression with patient and family, based on procedural outcomes

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes programmatic or institutional quality improvement initiatives (e.g., handwashing, reducing needle stick injuries)
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to the team (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in programmatic or institutional quality improvement initiatives
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community systems level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Identifies resources to meet the health needs of local communities and populations
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations and across health care delivery systems
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the resources of interprofessional teams
Participates in changing and adapting practice to provide for the needs of specific populations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of local population and community health needs
Reassesses patient and anticipates patient specific factors that may lead to readmission
Leads and role models effective coordination of patient-centered care among different disciplines and specialties
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the resources of interprofessional teams
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
Role models and advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations
Efficiently coordinates patient-centered care using interprofessional teams
Leads innovations and advocates across populations and communities with specific health care needs

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Identifies components of the complex health care system
Uses shared decision making in delivering care informed by patient- specific payment models
level_2: Describes basic health payment systems (e.g., private, public, government, and uninsured care) and different practice models (e.g., fee for service, capitated fees, accountable care organizations)
Adapts personal practice based on practice habits data
level_3: Describes the physician’s role and how the interrelated components of the complex health care system impact patient care
Advocates for patient care incorporating the limitations of their payment model (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources)
level_4: Describes the limitations of payment models and uses available patient care resources
Manages the interrelated components of complex health care systems for efficient and effective patient care
level_5: Analyzes how personal practice affects the system (e.g., length of stay, readmission rates, clinical efficiency)
Advocates for health policy to better align payment systems with high-value care

level_1: Demonstrates awareness of evidence- based practice parameters, how to access and use available evidence, and how to assess the quality of the evidence
level_2: Demonstrates critical thinking of clinical situations and incorporates patient preferences and values in evidence-based care plan for routine patients
level_3: Applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Navigates conflicting evidence to guide care tailored to individualized patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for the care of complex patients; and/or participates in the development of guidelines

level_1: Establishes personal and professional development goals and tracks own progress
Accurately self-assesses strengths, weaknesses, and opportunities for improvement
level_2: Seeks and is receptive to feedback
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and identifies when the plan should be modified
level_3: Recognizes when performance falls short of expectations and seeks feedback for improvement
Is able to coach others in the identification of gaps between knowledge and performance and formulate an improvement plan
level_4: Adapts behavior based on feedback
level_5: Seeks performance data with the intention to improve; independently creates and implements a learning plan

level_1: Identifies ethical decision-making skills specific to clinical work
Recognizes need to seek help from team members to manage and resolve complex ethical situations
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, and related topics
Demonstrates professional behavior in conflictual and/or stressful situations
level_3: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_4: Applies knowledge of ethical principles
Intervenes to prevent professional and ethical lapses in self and others
level_5: Demonstrates professional behavior in routine and complex situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution

level_1: Completes tasks and assigned responsibilities, with guidance
Admits errors and proposes remediation as necessary
level_2: Arrives on time and prepared for work
Proactively communicates with program staff members regarding situations that may impact own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Independently completes tasks and assigned responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in routine situations
Intervenes in situations that impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_4: Takes responsibility for personal actions and performance
level_5: Independently completes tasks and assigned responsibilities in a timely manner with appropriate attention to detail in complex or stressful situations

level_1: Recognizes status of personal and professional well-being, with assistance
With assistance, proposes a plan to remediate or improve limits in the knowledge/skills of self or team
level_2: Recognizes limits in the knowledge/skills of self, with assistance
Independently develops a plan to optimize lifelong personal and professional well-being
level_3: Independently recognizes status of personal and professional well-being
Independently develops a plan to remediate or improve limits in the knowledge/skills of self or team
level_4: Independently recognizes limits and the knowledge/skills of self or team and demonstrates appropriate help-seeking behaviors
Coaches others when emotional responses or limitations in knowledge/skills do not meet professional expectations
level_5: With assistance, proposes a plan to optimize personal and professional well-being
Strives for self- improvement to provide the highest quality of patient care through lifelong learning and education

level_1: Uses language and nonverbal behavior to demonstrate respect and establish rapport
Organizes and initiates communication with patient/family to clarify expectations
Anticipates and consistently uses resources to ameliorate barriers in communication
level_2: Identifies common barriers to effective communication (e.g., language, disability) while accurately communicating own role within the health care system
Establishes a therapeutic relationship in challenging patient encounters
Independently, uses shared decision making to make a personalized care plan
level_3: Identifies the need to adjust communication strategies based on assessment of patient/family expectations
Identifies and uses available resources to ameliorate barriers in communication
Mentors others in situational awareness and critical self-reflection to consistently develop positive therapeutic relationships
level_4: Establishes a therapeutic relationship in straightforward encounters using active listening and clear language
With guidance, sensitively and compassionately delivers medical information and elicits patient/family values
Develops educational tools or methods to ameliorate communication barriers
level_5: Identifies complex barriers to effective communication (e.g., health literacy, cultural, bias)
Easily establishes therapeutic relationships, with attention to patient/family concerns and context, regardless of complexity
Role models shared decision making in patient/family communication, including those with a high degree of uncertainty/conflict

level_1: Respectfully requests a routine consultation
Solicits feedback on performance as a member of the health care team
Communicates feedback and constructive criticism to superiors
level_2: Uses language that values all members of the health care team
Checks own understanding of consultant recommendations
Role models flexible communication strategies that value input from all health care team members, resolving conflict when needed
level_3: Provides prompt, objective and honest feedback on evaluations
Uses active listening to adapt communication style to fit team needs
Facilitates regular health care team-based feedback in complex situations
level_4: Clearly and concisely explains clinical scenario and rationale for consultation
Communicates concerns and provides feedback to peers and learners
level_5: Communicates information effectively with all health care team members
Coordinates recommendations from different members of the health care team to optimize patient care

level_1: Accurately records information in the patient record
Uses documentation shortcuts accurately, appropriately, and in a timely manner
Provides guidance and feedback to other team members on ways to safeguard protected health information
level_2: Identifies and understands the importance of safeguarding protected health information
Concisely reports diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning in the patient record
Produces written or verbal communications (e.g., patient notes, e- mail) that serve as an example for others to follow
level_3: Documents required data in formats specified by institutional policy
Identifies breaches of protected health information and works to correct them
Provides feedback to improve others’ written communication
level_4: Demonstrates organized diagnostic and therapeutic reasoning through notes in the patient record
Appropriately selects direct (e.g. telephone, in- person) and indirect (e.g., progress notes, text messages, pager) forms of communication based on context and as required by institutional policy
Identifies potential systemic breaches of protected health information and works to correct them
level_5: Consistently safeguards protected health information
Communicates clearly, concisely, and in a timely manner, and in an organized written form, with anticipatory guidance
Identifies potential systemic gaps in communication and works to correct them
